_note: Global term dictionary. Short = 1-3 sentences, 20-45 words. link = deep section. cat = one of AI, MODEL, HARDWARE, SECURITY, SOFTWARE, PRODUCT, NETWORK.

local-ai.label: Local AI
local-ai.short: An AI assistant that runs its model on your own computer instead of sending your data to a server. You keep control of the model and the files.

local-first.label: Local-first
local-first.short: Designed to keep local tasks and data on your PC, while still allowing optional network-enabled features when you choose to use them.

local-inference.label: Local inference
local-inference.short: Running the AI model on your own hardware, rather than on a remote server. The response is produced on your machine.

inference.label: Inference
inference.short: The moment a model actually produces an answer from your input. On a local assistant it happens on your PC, using your CPU or GPU.

model.label: Model
model.short: The AI 'brain' — a large file that has learned patterns from text. You download one and it runs on your computer.

gguf.label: GGUF
gguf.short: A model file format commonly used for running AI models locally. It packages a model into a single file your PC can load.

quantization.label: Quantization
quantization.short: A way of compressing a model so it uses less memory and runs faster, at a small cost in quality. Q4 is a common middle ground.

context-window.label: Context window
context-window.short: How much text the model can consider at once. Larger windows let it handle longer documents and conversations.

token.label: Token
token.short: A small chunk of text — roughly part of a word — that the model reads and writes. Speed is usually measured in tokens per second.

embedding.label: Embedding
embedding.short: A numeric representation of meaning. It lets the assistant compare pieces of text by what they mean, not just the words used.

semantic-search.label: Semantic search
semantic-search.short: Search that looks for meaning and related concepts rather than only exact words. Useful when you remember the idea but not the wording.

llm.label: LLM
llm.short: Large Language Model — the kind of AI model that reads and writes text. Local models are smaller versions you can run yourself.

stt.label: Speech recognition
stt.short: Turning your spoken words into text. O.A.S.I.S. does this on your PC, so dictation works without sending audio anywhere.

tts.label: Speech synthesis
tts.short: Turning text into spoken audio. It lets the assistant answer out loud, in Spanish or English, using voices on your machine.

on-device.label: On-device
on-device.short: Work handled by your own computer's hardware instead of a remote server. Audio, images and text never have to leave the machine.

vision.label: Vision
vision.short: The ability to look at an image or your screen and describe what is there. It only happens when you ask.

ocr.label: OCR
ocr.short: Optical Character Recognition — reading text out of an image or a screenshot so the assistant can act on it or copy it.

wake-word.label: Wake word
wake-word.short: A short phrase that starts listening without touching the keyboard. Recognition runs locally, so the microphone is not streamed anywhere.

voice-cloning.label: Voice cloning
voice-cloning.short: Building a synthetic voice from a sample so replies sound like a chosen speaker. A Max feature, created from audio you provide yourself.

cpu.label: CPU
cpu.short: The main processor of your computer. It can run small AI models on its own, just more slowly than a graphics card.

gpu.label: GPU
gpu.short: A graphics card. For AI it acts as an accelerator, producing answers noticeably faster than the CPU alone.

vram.label: VRAM
vram.short: Memory available on a graphics card. Larger local models generally need more VRAM when running on the GPU.

ram.label: RAM
ram.short: Your computer's working memory. It holds the model while it runs, so more RAM lets you load larger models.

model-size.label: Model size
model-size.short: Usually written like '7B' — billions of parameters. Bigger models know more but need more memory and run slower.

offloading.label: Offloading
offloading.short: Splitting a model between your graphics card and your processor so it fits in the memory you have available.

permission.label: Permission
permission.short: Your per-tool setting that decides whether an action runs automatically, asks first, or is blocked. You can change it at any time.

sandbox.label: Sandbox
sandbox.short: An isolated environment used to run code with additional safety boundaries, so generated code cannot reach the rest of your system.

isolation.label: Isolation
isolation.short: Keeping an action inside its own contained environment, with limits on what it can read, write or reach.

high-impact.label: High-impact action
high-impact.short: An action that can change or remove things — like deleting files, running code or shutting down. These always ask for confirmation first.

audit-log.label: Action log
audit-log.short: A local record of what the assistant did, kept on your machine so you can review or undo recent actions.

telemetry.label: Telemetry
telemetry.short: Usage or crash data sent back to the maker. Here it ships off: nothing is reported unless you deliberately enable an outbound channel.

analytics.label: Analytics
analytics.short: Scripts that count visitors and behaviour. This site runs none, and the app has no analytics built in — there is nothing to opt out of.

encryption.label: Encryption
encryption.short: Scrambling stored data so only someone with the key can read it. Secrets and the local vault are encrypted on your machine.

vault.label: Vault
vault.short: The encrypted store for secrets such as API keys and tokens. It lives on your disk, not in a cloud account or a plain config file.

api.label: API
api.short: A defined way for two programs to talk to each other. Here it usually means the local interface other tools use to reach O.A.S.I.S.

mcp.label: MCP
mcp.short: A protocol that lets AI systems connect to external tools and services in a standardised way. It is how O.A.S.I.S. can use outside tool servers.

tool-server.label: Tool server
tool-server.short: An external service that offers extra tools to the assistant. You add it yourself, so it only runs when you configure it.

endpoint.label: Endpoint
endpoint.short: A specific address a program can send requests to. With telemetry off, there is no endpoint receiving your data by default.

webhook.label: Webhook
webhook.short: A URL that receives a message when something happens. O.A.S.I.S. only uses one if you set it up for diagnostics.

localhost.label: Localhost
localhost.short: Your own machine as seen by itself. The app's internal server listens there, so nothing is exposed on your network.

network.label: Network features
network.short: The optional parts that reach the internet, such as web search and integrations. They only communicate when you use or configure them.

server.label: Server
server.short: A remote computer that answers requests. A local assistant avoids depending on one for chat, voice or memory.

cloud.label: Cloud
cloud.short: Computing that runs on someone else's servers over the internet. Here it is the alternative the app is built to avoid for everyday tasks.

offline.label: Offline
offline.short: Working with no internet connection at all. Once a model is downloaded, chat, voice, memory and local tools keep running.

offline-first.label: Offline-first
offline-first.short: Built so the core experience works without a connection, and network access is an extra you opt into — not a requirement to function.

open-source.label: Open source
open-source.short: Software whose source code is published for anyone to read and modify. O.A.S.I.S. is not: it is proprietary, with a public changelog instead.

proprietary.label: Proprietary
proprietary.short: Software whose source code is not public and is licensed by its owner. The app is proprietary; the AI models you run are licensed separately.

eula.label: EULA
eula.short: End User Licence Agreement — the terms you accept to install and use the app. It ships with the installer and covers one Windows machine.

docker.label: Docker
docker.short: A tool that runs software in isolated containers. O.A.S.I.S. uses it to execute generated code safely, and it is optional.

ollama.label: Ollama
ollama.short: A popular way to run local models from a command line. It is strong as a model server; O.A.S.I.S. is the assistant layer around a model.

lm-studio.label: LM Studio
lm-studio.short: A desktop app for downloading and chatting with local models. Excellent for a chat window; it does not drive your PC or keep a memory of you.

llama-cpp.label: llama.cpp
llama-cpp.short: A widely used local runtime that loads GGUF models and runs them efficiently on CPUs and GPUs. It is the engine under many local AI tools.

hugging-face.label: Hugging Face
hugging-face.short: A large public catalogue of AI models. The app searches it so you can pick a compatible model and download it without hunting for files.

database.label: Local database
database.short: The file on your disk where memory is stored — messages, notes and documents, indexed so they can be found again by meaning.

hash.label: SHA-256 hash
hash.short: A short fingerprint of a file. Comparing it with the published value proves the installer you downloaded is the one that was released.

runtime.label: Runtime
runtime.short: The engine that actually loads a model file and produces answers. It is what turns a downloaded file into a working assistant.

repository.label: Repository
repository.short: The public project folder on GitHub, where releases, the roadmap and the changelog live.

agent.label: Agent
agent.short: An assistant that does more than answer: it plans, uses tools, asks for permission and verifies the result.

workflow.label: Workflow
workflow.short: A routine you describe in plain words, like 'every day at 9 send me a briefing', that runs on a schedule.

memory.label: Memory
memory.short: What the assistant keeps between conversations — facts, notes and documents — stored on your disk and searchable by meaning.

persistent-memory.label: Persistent memory
persistent-memory.short: Information that survives after the conversation ends, so you don't have to repeat yourself every time.

skill.label: Skill
skill.short: A small piece of behaviour triggered by your phrases, so common requests get handled your way.

companion.label: Companion
companion.short: Optional apps that reach your assistant from elsewhere — phone, browser or chat platforms — over your own network.

browser-extension.label: Browser extension
browser-extension.short: A Max add-on that lets the browser talk to your assistant on the same PC, so it can work with the page you are looking at.

integration.label: Integration
integration.short: A connection to an outside service, like a messaging platform. It only communicates when you enable and use it.

tool.label: Tool
tool.short: A single capability the assistant can use — reading a file, changing the volume, setting a timer — each with its own permission level.

personal.label: Personal
personal.short: The free plan: local chat, voice, memory, documents and everyday PC control, with no account and no message limits.

max.label: Max
max.short: The paid edition: advanced coding, sandboxed execution, workflows, integrations and companion apps. A one-time payment, not a subscription.
